area: Zeiler implementation conventions: the shared brief for engineers building all seven features
harbor_approach:
Harbor's conventions are mostly the opposite of Zeiler's. Zeiler deliberately takes the security-heavier route, so engineers should borrow Harbor's UI and feature ideas but not its plumbing.

- PERSISTENCE: almost entirely browser localStorage in the webview. Keys look like `harbor.<domain>[.vN]`: `harbor.settings` (src/lib/settings.tsx:196, read at :392, written at :529), `harbor.profiles.v1`, `harbor.player.prefs.v1`, `harbor.library.local.v1`, `harbor.watchlist.v1`, `harbor.picker-cache.v5`, `harbor.iptv.favorites.v2` (grep across src/lib/*.ts*). Schema changes bump the key suffix (.v4 to .v5). src/lib/storage-recovery.ts (`setItemWithRecovery`, `PRUNABLE_KEYS_IN_ORDER`) frees space when the quota runs out by dropping caches.
- IPC: about 79 commands, all in one `tauri::generate_handler!` in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:274. They are defined across flat per-feature modules (src-tauri/src/mpv.rs, cast.rs, dvr.rs, stream_proxy.rs, …) with the error type `Result<T, String>` (e.g. lib.rs:29 `deeplink_set_stremio`). Command names carry a `harbor_` prefix or a feature prefix.
- NETWORK: the frontend makes HTTP calls itself through tauri-plugin-http (src/lib/safe-fetch.ts).
- SECURITY CONFIG (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json): `csp: null`, and assetProtocol scope `**`.
- CAPABILITIES (src-tauri/capabilities/default.json): grants `http:default` for `https://*/*` and `http://*/*`, `fs:allow-write-file` on `**`, dialog, `shell:allow-execute` for a yt-dlp sidecar, process and updater. They apply to four windows: main, harbor-pip, harbor-browser, harbor-modal-overlay.
- DEEP LINKS: harbor:// and stremio:// are registered.
- FRONTEND LAYOUT: feature folders (src/lib/<feature>/, src/views/<feature>/, src/components/<feature>/).
- NAVIGATION: a frame stack in src/lib/view.tsx:57-76 whose Frame union includes `player` (the player is a stack frame, so the shell state survives playback), plus `addon-detail`, `live`, `calendar`, `person` and `service`.
zeiler_today:
ZEILER TODAY (read end to end; file paths are under /home/user/sailor)

Every claim below was checked against the source tree.

1) PERSISTENCE
- Who owns it: all persisted state is owned by Rust. There is no localStorage, sessionStorage or IndexedDB anywhere in src/.
- Startup (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:43-46): `AppState::load(app_data_dir, app_cache_dir)` runs inside `.setup()`.
- Files in the data dir (identifier `io.zeiler.desktop`):
  - `settings.json`: the `Settings` struct (state.rs:15-58), with `#[serde(rename_all="camelCase", default)]`
  - `addons.json`: `Vec<Descriptor>`, the user's addons in install order
  - `engine/`: librqbit DHT persistence, `engine/dht.json`. Session persistence is deliberately off (zeiler-engine/src/engine.rs:109-133).
- Files in the cache dir:
  - `torrents/`: one folder per infohash
  - `updates/<ver>.pkg`: written by updater.rs
- Window geometry is handled by tauri-plugin-window-state.
- I/O helpers: private `read_json` / `write_json` (state.rs:207-242).
  - A missing file means defaults.
  - A corrupt file is renamed to `*.json.corrupt.bak` and replaced by defaults.
  - Any other IO error fails startup.
  - Writes are atomic: `*.json.tmp`, then rename.
  - All writes are serialized by one global `persist_lock` (state.rs:118, 192, 198).
- Schema versioning: none. There is no version field and no wrapper object. Settings evolve additively through struct-level `default`; unknown keys are ignored on read and dropped on the next write.
- Migration precedent: `migrate_legacy_data` (state.rs:80-106) copies `MIGRATED_FILES` from the pre-rename `app.sailor.desktop` folder. It has unit tests that use temp dirs.
- Built-in addons: `effective_addons()` (state.rs:147-163) puts the compiled-in Cinemeta snapshot (`src-tauri/builtin/cinemeta-manifest.json`, `CINEMETA_TRANSPORT_URL`) in front when `settings.builtin_cinemeta` is on. It is flagged `official` + `protected`, and the UI shows it as "Built-in".

2) IPC (Rust side)
- Domain modules: `src-tauri/src/commands/{addons,content,engine,player,mpv,settings}.rs`, declared in commands/mod.rs. updater.rs sits beside them.
- Naming: snake_case `<domain>_<verb>`, e.g. `addon_preview`, `catalog_load`, `meta_get`, `streams_get`, `engine_resolve`, `player_embedded_set_property`, `settings_set`, `update_check`.
- Shape: every command is `#[tauri::command] pub async fn …`. It takes `State<'_, AppState>` (or the separately managed `tauri::State<'_, commands::mpv::PlayerState>`, or `AppHandle`) and returns `Result<T, IpcError>`. Tauri 2 requires a Result for async commands that borrow State.
- Errors: `IpcError` (error.rs) is a thiserror + serde enum `#[serde(tag="kind", content="message", rename_all="camelCase")]` with variants InvalidInput, Addon, NotFound, Engine, Player, Storage. It has `From<AddonError>` and `From<PlayerError>`; engine anyhow errors are mapped with `format!("{e:#}")`.
- Registration: commands are listed by full path in the single `generate_handler!` (lib.rs:54-77). Managed state goes in through `app.manage` (lib.rs:46, 49).
- Payloads: IPC structs use `#[serde(rename_all="camelCase")]`. Struct arguments are wrapped in a named parameter (`CatalogArgs` as `args`, `TorrentStreamRequest` as `request`, `PlaybackRequest` as `request`). Top-level params are snake_case in Rust and camelCase in JS (Tauri converts automatically).
- Events: named `<domain>://<event>`, i.e. `player://event` (kebab-case tagged `PlayerEvent`, embedded.rs:70-93) and `update://ready|installing|failed`. There are no Channels yet; ARCHITECTURE plans them for high-frequency data.
- Security patterns: scheme allow-listing (`check_scheme` in mpv.rs:60, a duplicate in player.rs). mpv property and command allow-lists are `PROPERTY_ALLOW` (mpv.rs:43) and `COMMAND_ALLOW` (mpv.rs:58). Credentials are redacted with `zeiler_player::redact_url`.

3) IPC (TS side)
- src/lib/ipc.ts: one-line arrow exports `export const addonAdd = (url) => invoke<Descriptor>("addon_add", { url })`, plus the helpers `errorMessage` and `errorKind`.
- src/lib/types.ts: hand-written mirrors of the Rust types. `Option<T>` becomes `?: T | null`. The `Settings` mirror is at :180 and the `IpcError` kind union at :200.
- src/lib/player-ipc.ts: deliberately self-contained, duplicating some wrappers. Its `ResolvedStream` is out of date: it declares `fileName/fileLength`, while Rust sends `fileIdx/fileName/fileSize`.

4) FRONTEND ROUTING (src/lib/view.tsx)
- No router library. A `Frame[]` stack lives in React context, capped by `STACK_MAX=30`.
- Root views: `RootView` union and `ROOT_VIEWS` array (home, discover, movies, shows, anime, library, addons, settings). `setView` resets the stack; settings pushes on top instead.
- Overlay frames: `meta | filter | picker`, opened with `openMeta` / `openFilter` / `openPicker`. Escape pops them (view.tsx:102-118).
- src/App.tsx `Shell`:
  - `hideSidebar` for picker/settings
  - an `overlays` filter on the kinds meta/filter/picker/settings
  - a `RootViewHost` switch
  - an `OverlayFrame` switch
  - Neither switch has an exhaustiveness check.
- Player route: `#/player?url=…|infoHash=…` is a separate hash route in src/main.tsx. It swaps out the whole App, outside StrictMode and outside StoreProvider/ViewProvider, so the webview background can be transparent over mpv's child HWND. Entering it unmounts the shell, and the view stack is lost on return.
- Nothing in the UI navigates to `#/player` today. PlayPicker.tsx:86-140 still launches external mpv through `playerPlay`; the route is reachable only through `VITE_ZEILER_AUTOPLAY`.

5) GLOBAL STORE (src/lib/store.tsx)
- `StoreProvider` combines three contexts:
  - `useAddons()`: {addons, loaded, reload}
  - `useSettings()`: {settings, save(patch)}. `save` is an optimistic, shallow merge `{...settings, ...patch}` that sends the whole object to `settings_set`, reverts silently on error, and calls `applyTheme`.
  - `useSearch()`: {open, setOpen}

6) DESIGN SYSTEM
- Tokens: Tailwind 4 `@theme` tokens in src/index.css (canvas, surface, elevated, raised, ink, ink-muted, ink-subtle, edge, edge-soft, accent, accent-soft, danger; radii; font-display (serif), font-sans, font-mono; `animate-fade-in|step-in|modal-in|nudge-in|popover-in|loader-pulse`; `.no-scrollbar`).
- Themes: src/lib/theme.ts presets override the 12 `--color-*` tokens inline (`ALL_TOKENS`).
- src/components/ui.tsx: Spinner, ErrorNote, EmptyState, Badge(tone default|warn|good|accent), Modal(title,onClose,wide), CopyField, SectionCard, Toggle, ToggleRow(lockReason), ChipPicker<T>, ComingLaterBlock.
- src/components/cards.tsx: PickCard, TopRankCard, AddonLogo.
- Other building blocks:
  - Poster(+fallbackGradient)
  - Row: a rail with `min` cell width and `onEndReached`
  - HeroCarousel(variant card|bleed)
  - GenreTiles
  - RowSkeletons, oddly exported from views/Home.tsx
  - lib/rows.ts: useCatalogRows, dedupRows
  - lib/catalogs.ts: browsableCatalogs, searchableCatalogs, genreOptions, extraProps
- Icons: lucide-react.

7) TESTING
- Rust: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of each file, with inline raw-JSON fixtures that mirror real addon output (manifest.rs, resource.rs, request.rs, fanout.rs, magnet.rs, zeiler-player lib.rs, state.rs). `#[tokio::test]` for async code. `.invalid` hosts guarantee no network. Temp dirs are named `zeiler-<test>-<pid>`.
- Live network tests: crates/zeiler-addon/tests/live.rs with `#[ignore = "network"]`.
- Frontend: no test runner, no ESLint, no Prettier. The only gate is `tsc --noEmit` (strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters).

8) CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- Rust job on ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest and macos-latest:
  1. npm ci
  2. `npm run build` (required because `tauri::generate_context!` needs ../dist)
  3. toolchain 1.99.0
  4. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
  5. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
  6. `cargo test --workspace --locked`
- Frontend job: `npm run typecheck`.
- The `embedded` feature is never built in CI, so zeiler-player/src/embedded.rs (and its tests) and the Windows `imp` in commands/mpv.rs are not compiled there.
- cargo-deny (deny.toml: a license allow-list, unknown git sources denied, only rqbit's git allowed) is not run in CI.

9) CSP AND CAPABILITIES (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:27-40, capabilities/default.json)
- CSP:
  - `connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost`, so the webview cannot fetch remote URLs
  - `img-src 'self' data: blob: https: http:`
  - `media-src 'self'`
  - `frame-src 'none'`
  - `script-src 'self'`
  - `font-src 'self' data:`
- Capabilities: only window `main`, with core:default, window controls (drag, minimize, toggle-maximize, close, set-fullscreen, is-fullscreen), `opener:default` (http/https/mailto/tel) and `deep-link:default`. There is no fs, dialog, http or shell plugin.
- Deep links: `deep-link.desktop.schemes: []`, and no incoming-link handler exists.
- Window: `decorations: false`, with custom chrome using `data-tauri-drag-region` (Topbar.tsx and Sidebar.tsx).
gaps: No schema versioning on settings.json or addons.json. Settings can only grow by adding fields: changing the type of an existing field makes the whole file fail to parse, `read_json` moves it to settings.json.corrupt.bak, and every user setting resets to its default (state.rs:207-228).

`read_json`/`write_json` are private to state.rs, and AppState is a single struct with one global persist_lock. Every feature that needs storage (library, account, profile, subtitle prefs, skip prefs) would edit state.rs, the biggest merge hotspot.

No reusable registry for built-in addons. `effective_addons()` hard-codes Cinemeta plus the `builtin_cinemeta` toggle (state.rs:60-78, 147-163). Built-in OpenSubtitles would copy-paste this unless it is generalized first.
Nowhere to keep secrets. The whole `Settings` object goes to the webview through `settings_get` and is held in React context, so an auth key stored in settings.json would leak into the UI layer.

No Rust HTTP client for APIs other than addons. `AddonClient` is GET-only, sends no custom headers, and its `get_json` is private (zeiler-addon/src/client.rs). Stremio API calls (POST JSON), subtitle hashing or intro-timestamp APIs need a new client, and the CSP forbids doing them from the webview.

The player route `#/player` replaces App (src/main.tsx:10-24), so the view stack and store are lost when playback starts and reloaded from scratch on return. PlayPicker never navigates there anyway: it still calls external `player_play`.

Type and doc drift. In player-ipc.ts, `ResolvedStream` has `fileLength` while Rust sends `fileSize`/`fileIdx`. The docs/ARCHITECTURE.md IPC list says `engine_stats {torrentId}` and `engine_remove {torrentId,…}` (the code uses `infoHash`) and omits `player_stop`, `update_*` and `player_embedded_*`.

`RootViewHost` and `OverlayFrame` in App.tsx have no exhaustive `never` check. A new RootView or Frame kind that is not wired into both switches, the `overlays` filter (App.tsx:33-35) and the Escape kinds (view.tsx:110) renders nothing, with no type error.
No frontend unit tests, linter or formatter. tsc is the only frontend gate.

The `embedded` feature code (zeiler-player/src/embedded.rs and its tests, plus the Windows `imp` module in src-tauri/src/commands/mpv.rs) is never compiled or tested in CI. cargo-deny is not in CI either.
No subscription mechanism beyond `app.emit` events. High-frequency streams (subtitle cues, skip-segment ticks) have no Channel pattern yet.
No file picking. There is no dialog plugin or capability, so a local subtitle file or avatar image needs a new capability (`dialog:allow-open`) or a Tauri drag-drop event.
Deep links are not wired: schemes are empty, and the single-instance callback ignores argv. stremio:// install links from a marketplace or website will not work.
`useSettings().save` merges shallowly and swallows errors. Nested settings objects must be passed whole, and a failed save is invisible to the user.

implementation_plan.step: Persistence rules for every new feature
implementation_plan.details:
WHERE:
- Durable state lives in Rust-owned JSON files under `app.path().app_data_dir()` (the `data_dir` passed to `AppState::load`).
- Re-creatable caches (artwork, subtitle downloads, segment caches) go under `app_cache_dir()`, in a feature subfolder such as `cache_dir/subtitles/`.
- Never use localStorage or sessionStorage. Zeiler has none, and Harbor's `harbor.*.vN` localStorage model is not adopted.

FORMAT:
- Pretty JSON, written atomically (`*.json.tmp`, then rename).
- On read: a missing file gives `T::default()`; a corrupt file is moved to `*.json.corrupt.bak` and replaced by defaults; any other IO error fails startup.

VERSIONING:
- settings.json is additive-only. New fields go in with defaults, and an existing field's name or type never changes. Wrap risky new nested fields with `#[serde_as(deserialize_as = "DefaultOnError")]`. serde_with is a workspace dependency but not yet a dependency of src-tauri, so add `serde_with = { workspace = true }` to src-tauri/Cargo.toml; Cargo.lock already contains it.
- Every NEW file uses an envelope, e.g. `{"version": 1, ...}`, read with `#[serde(default)]`, plus a `migrate(v)` match run at load time.
- Name files after the feature: `library.json`, `account.json`, `profile.json`. Do not add them to `MIGRATED_FILES`; that list exists only for the Sailor-era files.

SECRETS:
- A Stremio `authKey` or other tokens never go in settings.json, because settings_get mirrors it to the UI. Use a separate `account.json` that only Rust reads.
- Commands return a redacted profile (email, avatar, display name) and never the key.
- Never log keys or addon transport URLs; use `zeiler_player::redact_url`-style redaction.
- OS keyring storage would be a new dependency (e.g. the `keyring` crate, MIT/Apache) and is an owner decision; not assumed.

LOCKING:
- Clone a snapshot under a tokio RwLock, drop the guard, then await I/O or network. Follow the existing `effective_addons()` and `persist_addons()` pattern.
- Mutate inside a scoped `{ let mut g = x.write().await; … }` block before calling persist.

implementation_plan.step: Step 0 PR (land before the parallel feature PRs): pull the shared choke points apart
implementation_plan.details:
One small PR, owned by one engineer and merged first.

(a) Move `read_json`/`write_json` into a new `src-tauri/src/persist.rs`, made `pub(crate)`, and add a generic `pub(crate) struct JsonStore<T> { path: PathBuf, value: RwLock<T>, lock: Mutex<()> }`:
- `async fn load(path) -> anyhow::Result<Self>`
- `async fn get(&self) -> T`, which clones
- `async fn update(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut T)) -> Result<T, IpcError>`, which mutates and then persists under its own lock

Keep the corrupt-file and atomic-write semantics and move their tests across. AppState keeps settings and addons. Each new feature then owns a `JsonStore<FeatureState>`, managed separately with `app.manage(...)` in lib.rs `.setup()`, so it never edits AppState.

(b) New `src-tauri/src/builtin.rs` holding a table, e.g. `struct Builtin { transport_url: &'static str, manifest_json: &'static str, enabled: fn(&Settings) -> bool }`. Snapshots live under `src-tauri/builtin/` (the existing cinemeta-manifest.json, and later the OpenSubtitles v3 manifest). `effective_addons()` iterates the table, keeps today's "skip if the user installed the same URL" rule, and flags each entry `official`/`protected`. Generalize the existing test `bundled_cinemeta_manifest_parses_and_serves_meta_for_imdb_ids` into one that runs over every built-in and asserts it does NOT support the `stream` resource. That test enforces the content-neutral policy in CI.

(c) Settings: reserve nested groups so features do not keep appending flat fields to the same lines. Add `pub subtitles: SubtitleSettings`, `pub skip: SkipSettings`, `pub profile: ProfileSettings` (each `#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all="camelCase", default)]`, defined in its feature's module or a `settings/` submodule), plus matching TS interfaces imported into the `Settings` mirror in types.ts. Feature owners then edit only their own struct.

(d) IpcError: if account sync needs it, add `Auth(String)` (e.g. a 401 or expired session) and `Network(String)`, and update the `IpcError.kind` union in src/lib/types.ts:200 in the same PR.

(e) App.tsx and view.tsx: add a `default: { const _x: never = view; return _x; }` exhaustiveness check to `RootViewHost` and `OverlayFrame`. Pre-register the planned RootViews (`live`, plus `profile`/`account` if it gets its own page) and Frames (`addon-detail` for the marketplace) with placeholder components, so later PRs only fill in components.

(f) Settings.tsx: change `SectionId`/`SECTIONS` so each section component is imported from `src/views/settings/<Name>Section.tsx`. Pre-register `subtitles`, `account` and `playback` (skip) ids.

(g) Fix the doc drift in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (`infoHash`, the full command list) and the `ResolvedStream` type in player-ipc.ts.

RUST: one module per domain at `src-tauri/src/commands/<domain>.rs`, plus a `pub mod <domain>;` line in commands/mod.rs (keep the list alphabetical). Template:
```rust
/// What it does and why (doc comment is mandatory house style).
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn library_list(state: State<'_, LibraryState>) -> Result<Vec<LibraryItem>, IpcError> { … }
```

RULES:
- Name: snake_case `<domain>_<verb>` (e.g. `account_login`, `account_logout`, `account_status`, `library_upsert`, `subtitles_get`, `skip_segments_get`, `addon_catalog_list`).
- Always `async` and always `Result<T, IpcError>`. Tauri requires a Result for async commands that borrow State.
- State access: use `State<'_, AppState>` for addons and settings, `State<'_, YourFeatureState>` for feature stores, and `AppHandle` when you need emit or path.
- Domain errors convert through `From` impls in error.rs or `.map_err(|e| IpcError::X(format!("{e:#}")))`. Messages are shown to the user as-is, so write full sentences.
- Payload structs: `#[derive(Serialize|Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`. Request structs go under one named parameter, e.g. `request: SubtitleQuery`, invoked as `{ request: {...} }`. Top-level parameters are snake_case in Rust and camelCase in JS (Tauri converts them).
- Validate untrusted input at the boundary: http(s) scheme checks, 40-char hex infohashes, allow-lists.

REGISTRATION: add the full path to the single `tauri::generate_handler![…]` in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:54-77. To limit conflicts, put each domain in its own contiguous block (blank line plus a `// <domain>` comment) instead of appending to the end. Feature state is registered with `app.manage(...)` inside `.setup()` next to lib.rs:46-49.

EVENTS:
- Name them `<domain>://<event>` (`account://changed`, `library://changed`), emitted with `app.emit(...)`. Rare notifications only; core:event:default already allows listen.
- For high-frequency data (subtitle cue ticks, skip countdown), follow the ARCHITECTURE plan and use a `tauri::ipc::Channel<T>` parameter, not events.

TS:
- Add one-line wrappers `export const libraryList = () => invoke<LibraryItem[]>("library_list");`. To avoid conflicts on ipc.ts and types.ts, put them in a new per-domain file `src/lib/<domain>-ipc.ts` that holds its own types, following the self-contained player-ipc.ts precedent.
- Edit the shared src/lib/types.ts only for cross-cutting types (Settings, IpcError, Stream, Subtitle).
- Errors: `catch (e) { setError(errorMessage(e)) }`, rendered with `<ErrorNote>`. Branch on `errorKind(e)` when needed.

DOCS: add the new commands to the 'Tauri IPC surface' list in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

implementation_plan.step: Network calls and new domain crates
implementation_plan.details:
The CSP has `connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost`, so ANY remote call has to be made in Rust and exposed as a command. That covers the Stremio account API, addon-collection sync, marketplace catalogs, OpenSubtitles, and intro/outro timestamp services.

Put protocol and HTTP logic in a domain crate that never depends on tauri, tested with plain `cargo test`:
- either a new `crates/zeiler-<name>` (e.g. `zeiler-account` for the Stremio API client)
- or a module inside `zeiler-addon` when it IS the addon protocol (e.g. the `addon_catalog` resource; `AddonCatalogResponse` already exists in resource.rs and Cinemeta's manifest already declares `addonCatalogs`)

A new crate is picked up by the workspace glob `crates/*`. It still needs an entry in `[workspace.dependencies]` in the root Cargo.toml plus the src-tauri/Cargo.toml dependency line. New crates use `version.workspace/edition.workspace/rust-version.workspace/license.workspace/authors.workspace`, i.e. GPL-3.0-or-later.

Client conventions, mirroring zeiler-addon/src/client.rs:
- one shared `reqwest::Client` with a `Zeiler/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>` user agent
- connect timeout 10 s, total timeout 30 s, at most 10 redirects, gzip
- a streamed response-size cap
- lenient serde (`DefaultOnError`, `DefaultOnNull`, `VecSkipError`, the custom number-or-string deserializers)
- per-call timeouts as module constants (as in content.rs `META_TIMEOUT`/`STREAMS_TIMEOUT`)
- no cookies; never log URLs that may carry credentials

Do NOT add auth headers to `AddonClient`: by design it never sends custom headers.

Policy: built-ins and seeded defaults may only be metadata or subtitle addons. Never seed a stream addon.

Privacy: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (Security posture) says addon transport URLs are 'never sent anywhere but the addon host'. Syncing the addon collection to a Stremio account breaks that unless it is explicit opt-in with an updated doc.

ADD A SIDEBAR PAGE (RootView):
1. src/lib/view.tsx: add the name to the `RootView` union and the `ROOT_VIEWS` array.
2. src/App.tsx: add a case to `RootViewHost`.
3. src/chrome/Sidebar.tsx: add a `NavEntry` to `primary` or `collections` (lucide icon, size 20, strokeWidth 1.7). Live TV already has a disabled placeholder entry pointing to `home`: change its `view` to `live` and drop `disabled`.
4. Layout: a root page renders `<main className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-12 pb-20 pt-28">` (the top padding clears the fixed 80 px Topbar), or a full-bleed `relative h-full overflow-y-auto bg-canvas` as in TypeRoom.

ADD AN OVERLAY (Frame, e.g. `{ kind: "addon-detail"; descriptor: Descriptor }`):
1. view.tsx: add the variant to the `Frame` union, add an `openX` to `ViewCtx` and its `useMemo` value, and add the kind to the Escape list (view.tsx:110).
2. App.tsx: add the kind to the `overlays` filter (:33-35) and a case to `OverlayFrame`.
3. If side chrome should hide, extend `hideSidebar` (App.tsx:30) and Topbar's `top.kind === "picker"` early return.
4. Layout: an overlay renders `<main className="absolute inset-0 z-30 overflow-y-auto bg-canvas">`.

CATALOG ROOMS for anime, live TV and other types: reuse TypeRoom.tsx's `ROOMS` config (types array, hero variant, copy), `browsableCatalogs(addons).filter(type)`, `useCatalogRows`, `dedupRows`, `Row`/`PickCard`/`TopRankCard`/`HeroCarousel`. Genre browsing goes through `openFilter(type, genre)` and FilterView.

PLAYER: `#/player?...` is a separate hash route (src/main.tsx) that unmounts the shell. To start playback, set `window.location.hash = "#/player?" + params` (params documented in pages/Player.tsx:10-14); return with `history.back()`. Before wiring PlayPicker to it, the player owner must either persist the view stack across the swap (e.g. a module-level or sessionStorage snapshot that ViewProvider restores; per-viewer convenience only), or make the player a Frame as Harbor does (view.tsx:76 `{kind: "player"}`) while keeping the transparent-background trick.

The player page has no access to `useSettings`/`useView`. It must use player-ipc.ts plus direct `settings_get`.

Z-INDEX LADDER (stay inside it):
- overlays z-30
- settings overlay z-40

implementation_plan.step: Global store and settings UI recipe
implementation_plan.details:
src/lib/store.tsx has three contexts: `useAddons()` {addons, loaded, reload}, `useSettings()` {settings, save(patch)} and `useSearch()`.

NEW GLOBAL STATE (account or profile, library): create its own provider file, e.g. `src/lib/account.tsx` exporting `AccountProvider` and `useAccount()`. Load it once in a `useEffect`, re-fetch on its `<domain>://changed` event, and nest it in App.tsx inside `<StoreProvider>`. That is a one-line edit; do not grow store.tsx.

SETTINGS: `save()` merges shallowly and sends the WHOLE Settings object, so for nested groups always write `save({ subtitles: { ...settings.subtitles, size: 120 } })`. It reverts silently on failure; when an error matters, call the command directly and show `<ErrorNote>`.

Settings whose effect lands on a running subsystem: the existing precedent is `settings_set` calling `player.relocate`. For mpv subtitle style, apply the values from the player page through allow-listed property sets, rather than adding more side effects to `settings_set`.

SETTINGS PAGE: after Step 0, add a section by creating `src/views/settings/<X>Section.tsx` built from `SectionCard`, `ToggleRow` (with `lockReason` for gated options), `ChipPicker`, and the input recipe below. Then add one entry to `SECTIONS` (group, id, label, lucide icon, sub) and one render line.

When adding a Settings field:
- Rust: state.rs `Settings`, plus its Default (or the nested struct's derive(Default)).
- TS: the `Settings` interface in src/lib/types.ts (or the nested interface).

TOKENS (src/index.css @theme):
- Colors only through tokens: `bg-canvas|surface|elevated|raised`, `text-ink|ink-muted|ink-subtle`, `border-edge|edge-soft`, `bg-accent/15 text-accent`, `bg-danger/15 border-danger/30`. Two literal exceptions are already in use: warning text `text-[oklch(0.75_0.12_25)]` and IMDb yellow.
- A NEW color token must go in `@theme`, `ALL_TOKENS` in src/lib/theme.ts, and every preset (or deliberately fall back), otherwise themes will not re-tint it.

TYPOGRAPHY:
- Page kicker: `text-[11px] font-bold uppercase tracking-[0.42em] text-ink-subtle`
- H1: `font-display text-[44px] font-medium leading-[1.05] tracking-tight text-ink`
- Subtitle: `text-[15px] text-ink-muted`
- Section heading: `text-[19px] font-medium tracking-tight`
- Field label: `text-[12px] font-medium uppercase tracking-[0.14em] text-ink-subtle`

BUTTONS:
- Primary: `h-12 rounded-xl bg-ink px-6 text-[13.5px] font-semibold text-canvas transition-transform hover:scale-[1.02] active:scale-[0.97] disabled:opacity-50`
- Pill CTA: `h-11 rounded-full bg-ink px-6 text-[14px] font-semibold text-canvas hover:scale-[1.03]`
- Secondary: `h-10 rounded-xl border border-edge-soft px-4 text-[12.5px] font-medium text-ink-muted hover:border-edge hover:text-ink`
- Destructive: AddonCard's Remove button (Addons.tsx)

OTHER RECIPES:
- Input: `h-12 w-full rounded-xl border border-edge bg-canvas px-4 text-[14px] text-ink outline-none placeholder:text-ink-subtle focus:border-ink`
- List card: `rounded-2xl border border-edge-soft bg-elevated/40 px-5 py-4`
- Motion: `animate-modal-in`, `animate-nudge-in`, `animate-popover-in`; `.no-scrollbar` for rails.

COMPONENTS (src/components):
- ui.tsx: Spinner, ErrorNote, EmptyState, Badge, Modal, CopyField, SectionCard, Toggle, ToggleRow, ChipPicker, ComingLaterBlock
- cards.tsx: PickCard, TopRankCard, AddonLogo (the marketplace grid should reuse AddonLogo plus the Addons.tsx `AddonSummary` install-confirm modal)
- Poster (and fallbackGradient), Row, HeroCarousel, GenreTiles, RowSkeletons
- Player chrome lives in pages/Player.tsx: SeekBar, VolumeControl, TrackMenu, TorrentStats

MPV SURFACE: the video area must paint nothing (transparent document background), and controls are overlays.

CODE STYLE: named function-component exports; inline-typed props; discriminated-union local state (`Phase` with `kind`); `useEffect` cancellation with a `let cancelled = false` cleanup; a request-id ref for debounced queries; `void promise` for fire-and-forget calls; files in views/ are PascalCase.tsx, files in lib/ are kebab-case.ts; 2-space indent, double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas.

ATTRIBUTION: any recipe ported from Harbor keeps an MIT note in the file header and gets an entry in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.

RUST UNIT TESTS: every new parser or protocol file gets a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom.
- Inline raw-JSON fixtures copied from REAL service output (as in manifest.rs, resource.rs).
- Cover lenient parsing: nulls, numbers as strings, unknown fields, invalid list items skipped.
- Cover URL building with byte-exact expectations (request.rs style).
- Async code uses `#[tokio::test]`.
- Tests must never touch the network. Use `https://addon.invalid/...` hosts (fanout.rs) or a pure function seam.
- Filesystem tests use `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("zeiler-{test}-{}", std::process::id()))` and clean up first (state.rs tests).
- Security rules get explicit tests: scheme rejection, allow-list refusal, secrets never in argv/logs (see zeiler-player `builds_args_with_headers_and_title_but_no_url`).

LIVE TESTS: one per external service, in `crates/<crate>/tests/live.rs`, each marked `#[tokio::test] #[ignore = "network"]`, run with `cargo test -p <crate> --test live -- --ignored`. A live test that needs credentials must read them from env vars and skip when they are absent; never commit keys.

NO TAURI IN TESTS: keep logic in domain crates or plain functions so it is testable without a running app. Command functions themselves stay thin.

EMBEDDED PLAYER: the `embedded` feature is not built in CI. On Windows, run `node scripts/fetch-libmpv.mjs`, then `cargo clippy -p zeiler --features embedded -- -D warnings` (`ZEILER_SKIP_LIBMPV_CHECK=1` skips the mpv.lib check for non-linking runs) and `cargo test -p zeiler-player --features embedded`. Building it on Linux needs the libmpv dev package, which this container lacks; untested.

FRONTEND: no test runner exists. Keep logic either in Rust or in small pure TS helpers (as in lib/catalogs.ts). Adding vitest would be a separate PR touching package.json, package-lock.json and ci.yml.

implementation_plan.step: CI gates and local pre-push checklist
implementation_plan.details:
CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs Rust on ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest and macos-latest. Run these locally, in this order:
1. `npm ci`
2. `npm run build`, because `tauri::generate_context!` needs `../dist`; clippy and test fail in a fresh checkout without it
3. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (rustfmt.toml: edition 2024, Unix newlines, default 100 cols)
4. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
5. `cargo test --workspace --locked`
6. `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` with strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters)

The toolchain is pinned to 1.99.0 (rust-toolchain.toml) and the MSRV field is 1.90; edition 2024 let-chains and let-else are in use.

`--locked` means Cargo.lock must be committed with any dependency change, and package-lock.json likewise for `npm ci`. On a Cargo.lock merge conflict, take main's lockfile and re-run `cargo build`/`cargo check` to re-resolve. Do not hand-merge it.

Clippy runs on three OSes, so OS- or feature-gated code needs the stub-module pattern from commands/mpv.rs: `#[cfg(all(windows, feature="embedded"))] mod imp` plus a `#[cfg(not(...))] mod imp` stub with the same signatures, and `cfg_attr(..., allow(dead_code))` for fields only the real implementation reads.

Also run `cargo deny check` manually when adding dependencies (it is not in CI):
- the license allow-list in deny.toml must cover the new crate
- git dependencies other than rqbit are denied

Never bump versions in feature PRs. The workspace version 0.1.3 in Cargo.toml, package.json and tauri.release.conf.json flows are release-only.

Commit style (CONTRIBUTING.md): imperative mood, the 'why' in the body, one change per PR, refactors separate from behavior changes.

implementation_plan.step: CSP, capability and window constraints for new features
implementation_plan.details:
CSP (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:27-40):
- No fetch or XHR from the webview to any remote host; use Rust commands.
- Remote images are fine (`img-src https: http: data: blob:`): avatars, addon logos, posters.
- `media-src 'self'`: no remote `<video>/<audio>/<track>`. Subtitles are rendered by mpv (`sid`, the `sub-*` properties), or by HTML overlay text that Rust has already fetched and parsed and sent over IPC.
- `frame-src 'none'`: no iframes. Addon configure pages, Stremio web login and YouTube embeds open in the system browser through `openUrl` from `@tauri-apps/plugin-opener`, which `opener:default` permits for http/https.
- `script-src 'self'` and `font-src 'self' data:`: no remote SDKs or web fonts; bundle any font.
- Treat relaxing the CSP as a security-review change; Harbor's `csp: null` is not adopted.

CAPABILITIES (src-tauri/capabilities/default.json): only window `main`, core defaults, window controls, `opener:default`, `deep-link:default`.
- JS cannot create windows (no `core:window:allow-create`/`core:webview:allow-create-webview-window`).
- Any new window must be created from Rust AND have its label added to `windows` to get IPC; prefer in-window overlays (the house pattern).
- Picking a local subtitle file needs either `tauri-plugin-dialog` with ONLY `dialog:allow-open` (a new dependency plus a capability edit), or Tauri's window drag-drop event (`dragDropEnabled` defaults to true; I have not verified it end to end).
- Adding `fs`, `http` or `shell` plugins is against the architecture's least-privilege stance.

MPV ALLOW-LISTS (src-tauri/src/commands/mpv.rs:43-58):
- Subtitle styling needs extra properties in `PROPERTY_ALLOW` (e.g. `sub-font-size`, `sub-color`, `sub-border-color`, `sub-back-color`, `sub-font`, `sub-bold`, `secondary-sid`, `sub-ass-override`; check the names against the mpv manual).
- Skip intro/outro already works through `seek <sec> absolute`. Also observe `chapter-list`, which is already in `OBSERVED`/`JSON_PROPS` in embedded.rs:40-59.
- Do NOT add `sub-add`/`loadfile` to `COMMAND_ALLOW`; they take arbitrary paths or URLs. Write a dedicated command (e.g. `player_subtitle_add { url, title, lang }`) that applies the http(s) scheme check from `check_scheme`, or accepts a user-picked local path validated in Rust.

DEEP LINKS: schemes are `[]`. Registering `stremio://` for marketplace install links touches tauri.conf.json plus a Rust argv/deep-link handler, which must validate input and always route through the existing `addon_preview` confirm modal. ARCHITECTURE.md marks this as 'opt-in later'.

implementation_plan.step: Shared choke-point files: who touches them and how to extend each with minimal conflict
implementation_plan.details:
1. src-tauri/src/lib.rs (all features): add commands as a per-domain contiguous block inside `generate_handler!`, and `app.manage(FeatureState)` lines in `.setup()`. Never reorder existing lines.
2. src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs: one `pub mod` line per domain, alphabetical.
3. src-tauri/src/state.rs (persistence, built-ins, account, profile, subtitles, skip): after Step 0, edit only the nested Settings struct you own. New state goes in your own JsonStore, not AppState.
4. src-tauri/src/error.rs and the `IpcError` union in src/lib/types.ts: add kinds only in Step 0, or in a dedicated tiny PR.
5. src-tauri/src/commands/mpv.rs `PROPERTY_ALLOW`/`COMMAND_ALLOW` and crates/zeiler-player/src/embedded.rs `OBSERVED` (player, subtitles, skip): one entry per line, sorted within a commented group per feature. The subtitle and skip owners coordinate.
6. crates/zeiler-player/src/lib.rs `PlaybackRequest` (player, subtitles, resume): add fields only with the struct-level `default`. It also feeds `build_mpv_args`, so update its test.
7. crates/zeiler-addon/src/{lib.rs,resource.rs,manifest.rs} (catalogs, marketplace, subtitles): append re-exports, and add types in new sections with tests.
8. Cargo.toml, src-tauri/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock: add workspace dependencies in Step 0 if they are known up front; otherwise resolve lockfile conflicts by regenerating.
9. package.json and package-lock.json: avoid new npm dependencies; lucide-react and @tauri-apps/* already cover most needs.
10. src-tauri/tauri.conf.json and capabilities/default.json: one owner, security review required.
11. src/App.tsx: RootViewHost and OverlayFrame cases plus provider nesting; one line per addition.
12. src/lib/view.tsx: RootView, ROOT_VIEWS, Frame, the ViewCtx opener and the Escape list; pre-registered in Step 0.
13. src/lib/store.tsx: do not grow it; add sibling provider files.
14. src/lib/ipc.ts and src/lib/types.ts: per-domain `*-ipc.ts` files instead.
15. src/lib/player-ipc.ts and src/pages/Player.tsx (784 lines; embedded player, subtitles, skip, resume all touch it): the player owner first splits the chrome into `src/components/player/{SeekBar,VolumeControl,TrackMenu,TorrentStats}.tsx` and adds slots (`<SubtitlePanel/>`, `<SkipButton/>`) next to the TrackMenu row (Player.tsx:552-553). Subtitle and skip work then live in their own files.
16. src/main.tsx: player-route changes are owned by the player owner only.
17. src/chrome/Sidebar.tsx (catalogs/live, marketplace, profile): one `NavEntry` line each. src/chrome/Topbar.tsx (a profile avatar would go in the right-hand `justify-end` cluster before WindowControls).
18. src/views/Settings.tsx: after Step 0, one SECTIONS entry plus one render line per section.
19. src/views/Addons.tsx (marketplace, built-in OpenSubtitles): the marketplace becomes a tab or sub-view component in `src/views/addons/*`. Keep `AddonSummary` as the single install-confirm modal.
20. src/views/PlayPicker.tsx (embedded player hand-off, subtitles from `stream.subtitles`): owned by the player owner first.
21. src/index.css and src/lib/theme.ts: only for new tokens.
22. src-tauri/builtin/: one snapshot JSON per built-in, added through the Step 0 registry.
23. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (IPC list, Decisions, Security posture), CONTRIBUTING.md (built-in policy wording names only Cinemeta; update when OpenSubtitles lands), THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and README.md: append-only per feature.
24. .github/workflows/ci.yml: only for new gates (e.g. vitest or cargo-deny), in a dedicated PR.

implementation_plan.step: Recommended merge order to keep the seven features from colliding
implementation_plan.details:
1. Step 0 de-confliction PR: persist.rs, builtin.rs, nested Settings groups, IpcError kinds, view/App exhaustiveness, pre-registered RootViews/Frames/Settings sections, doc and type drift fixes.
2. Embedded player integration: split Player.tsx into components, decide the player-route state preservation, switch PlayPicker to the in-app route with external-mpv fallback.
3. In parallel after (2), each in its own files:
   - (a) subtitles: `player_subtitle_add`, extra allow-listed sub-* properties, a Settings subtitles section, `stream.subtitles` plus the subtitles-resource fan-out reusing the `aggregate_streams` pattern in fanout.rs
   - (b) skip intro/outro: chapter-list and/or an external segment source through a Rust command, and a `<SkipButton/>` slot
   - (c) built-in OpenSubtitles through the builtin registry; must be subtitles-only, enforced by the Step 0 test
4. Independent of the player, any time after Step 0:
   - (d) catalogs for all types: TypeRoom `ROOMS` entries for `tv`/`channel`/anime, Sidebar Live TV enabled, genre/filter views
   - (e) Stremio account plus profile: a new domain crate, `account.json` secret store, AccountProvider, a Settings 'account' section, a Topbar avatar; addon/library sync strictly opt-in
   - (f) addon marketplace: an `addon_catalog` command in zeiler-addon (resource already typed as `AddonCatalogResponse`), an `addon-detail` frame, install through the existing `addon_preview` confirm. Nothing is pre-installed, and no stream addon is ever seeded.

risks: Merge conflicts on the hot files (lib.rs handler list, state.rs Settings and AppState, view.tsx and App.tsx, Settings.tsx, Player.tsx, Cargo.lock) if seven features branch from today's main without the Step 0 de-confliction PR.

User data loss: changing the type or name of an existing Settings field, or adding a non-defaulted required field, sends settings.json to `.corrupt.bak` and resets every setting (state.rs:207-228). Keep evolution additive and defaulted.

Leaking secrets into the webview. Settings are mirrored wholesale to the UI, so an authKey placed in Settings would reach JS. Logging transport URLs or auth keys violates the ARCHITECTURE security posture.

Privacy-policy conflict: Stremio addon-collection or library sync would send addon transport URLs (which may embed credentials) to api.strem.io, contradicting docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ('never sent anywhere but the addon host'). It needs explicit opt-in, owner sign-off and a doc update.

Content-neutrality regressions: a built-in or marketplace default that serves `stream` resources violates CONTRIBUTING.md's non-negotiable rule. Enforce it with the Step 0 'no built-in supports stream' unit test. Whether the marketplace may even list third-party stream addons from addon catalogs is an owner decision; listing is not installing.

Security regressions from widening mpv allow-lists. `sub-add`, `loadfile` or `script` take arbitrary paths or URLs. Use dedicated, validated commands instead. Relaxing the CSP or adding fs/http/shell capabilities (as Harbor does) breaks the least-privilege model.
Player route state loss: navigating to `#/player` unmounts App and resets the view stack. Shipping the embedded player without fixing this makes 'Back' land on Home.
Windows-only and embedded-feature code is not compiled in CI, so clippy or test breakage there goes unnoticed until a manual Windows build.
Clippy runs with -D warnings on three OSes, so cfg-gated code that is fine on Windows can fail Linux or macOS with dead-code or unused warnings. Use the stub `mod imp` pattern.

Tauri argument-naming pitfalls: top-level params are converted camelCase to snake_case automatically, but nested struct fields need `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`. Mismatches fail only at runtime, because TS mirrors are hand-written and tsc cannot catch them.
React StrictMode double-invokes effects in dev for everything except the player page. New effects that start native resources (mpv, timers, subscriptions) must be idempotent and must clean up.

Some details are inferred rather than verified: the exact on-disk location of the window-state plugin file, whether the drag-drop event delivers usable file paths for local subtitles, and whether libmpv2 builds on Linux without libmpv dev headers.

harbor_files_to_adapt.why: Its Frame union (lines 57-76) makes the player a stack frame (`{kind: "player"}`) and has `addon-detail`, `live` and `calendar` frames. It shows how to keep shell state across playback, which Zeiler's separate `#/player` route loses. Adapt the idea (MIT, keep attribution) to the existing Zeiler view.tsx.

Reference only. Its versioned-key and prune-on-quota approach shows how Harbor evolves stored schemas (`.v1` to `.v5` key bumps). Zeiler keeps storage in Rust JSON files, but should copy the explicit per-store version idea through a `{version: N}` envelope in new files.

Counter-example. It lists the plugins, permissions and extra windows (http:*, fs:**, shell sidecar, pip, browser and modal-overlay windows) that Zeiler deliberately does NOT grant. Any Harbor feature port needing these must be redesigned to go through Rust commands.

verifiable_in_linux_container:
Partly.

What can be verified in this container:
- It has cargo/rustc, node 22 and npm, and pkg-config finds webkit2gtk-4.1, so the Linux gates can run: `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `npm run typecheck`.
- That covers all non-embedded Rust, the Step 0 refactors (persist.rs, builtin.rs with the no-stream test, nested Settings serde round-trips, migration tests) and TS type-checking.
- Opt-in live tests (`--ignored`) need outbound network through the proxy.

What cannot:
- The `embedded` feature: libmpv dev files are missing (`pkg-config mpv` fails), and the real `imp` module is Windows-only.
- Windows and macOS clippy differences.
- Runtime UI behavior (navigation, the transparent player route, CSP enforcement in a live webview), which needs a desktop session and a running Tauri app.
